body:
TUNGSTEN SESSION REPORT - 2026-09-05 (ledger session 138, WARRANT#455-469)

=== THE ONE SENTENCE ===
The compounding machinery is finished and it is NOT the constraint. Brackets, tiers, concurrency,
sizing and entry mechanics are all optimised around an edge of three percentage points. Everything
from here is win rate.

=== THE HEADLINE NUMBER ===
At 0.5 pips, best config TP4.0/SL4.0, tiers 90th/60th pct with half stake on tier B, 10 concurrent:
  10.3 trades/day, win rate 53.2%, 4,833 trades in sample
  UNLEVERED  +19.1% CAGR, 7.1% max drawdown
  LEVERED 5.6x to the 40% survival allowance: +100.8% CAGR
  100 DAYS FROM $100 -> $131.86   (unlevered $107.20)

=== WHY 5%/DAY IS NOT AVAILABLE (and what would make it so) ===
full Kelly on the measured edge      ~2.1%/day
  x survival rule c=0.20             ~0.76%/day    growth scales as c(2-c)=0.36
  x Wilson lower-bound sizing        ~0.28%/day
Two thirds of the loss is the >=60% capital rule, and it is not waste: full Kelly on this edge
carries a 60% chance of eventually being down 60%.
Kelly growth scales with the SQUARE of the edge, so 18x growth needs 4.25x the edge:
  53.2% win rate -> x2.0 over 250 days      58% -> x72       63.5% -> x160,881
+5%/day is not a leverage, frequency or compounding problem. It is a 10-point win-rate problem.

=== MAJOR RETRACTION OF MY OWN NUMBERS ===
An agent audit reproduced my pipeline and found:
 * my -0.06152 R headline does NOT reproduce: -0.11739 same-recipe, -0.21473 with an honest
   validation slice. I had chosen the EV floor BY READING THE TEST CURVE and reported that point.
 * effective sample is ~423 independent trades, not 9,261 (uniqueness 0.046-0.091).
 * MY BUG: adaptive_bracket.py fed the battery arange(n)*300 as timestamps, so higher-timeframe
   features straddled weekends and hour-of-day named hours that never happened. Real timestamps
   were the biggest single gain the audit found (+0.049 R).
   => CAPTURE 19.5% AND BELT L4 ARE WITHDRAWN. They rest on a fictitious calendar.
 * cleanest negative: holding geometry and side fixed, ranking bars by confidence gives
   z = -0.04, -0.77, -1.01, -0.12. Zero ability to rank moments. The "model chooses well" claim
   was geometry and the long-bias.

=== WHAT SURVIVED AND IS NEW ===
COST DECOMPOSITION: across 26 brackets, 97% of all net-R variation is the toll falling, 3% is edge
  rising. 0 of 26 brackets have a gross edge 2 SE from zero. Break-even spread 1.1-1.4 pips.

THE EDGE TRANSFERS (WARRANT#462): five instruments, both directions, leave-one-instrument-out, real
  timestamps. Positive lift on EVERY held-out pair: EURJPY +8.0%, EURUSD +10.3%, USDJPY +12.7%,
  GBPUSD +16.2%, USDCHF +28.4%. Strongest evidence the model learned price structure, not USDJPY.

SPREAD IS EVERYTHING (WARRANT#467): market entry by spread --
  2.0 pips: 0.4 trades/day, +0.8% CAGR   |   1.0: 4.0/day, +2.5%   |   0.8: 7.0/day, +4.5%
  0.6 pips: 12.0/day, +13.8%             |   0.4: 18.9/day, +44.6%
  Violently nonlinear because a lower spread makes far MORE trades pass the sizing test at all.
  At low spread MARKET entry beats LIMIT (60.0% vs 58.2% tier-A) -- the limit workaround was a
  workaround for an expensive broker.
  COMMISSION WARNING: an advertised 0.6-pip account usually adds ~$7/lot round turn (~0.7 pips),
  making the effective spread ~1.3. Ask for the all-in round-turn cost per standard lot.

DIVERSIFICATION (WARRANT#468): measured rho = +0.077 across the five pairs, far lower than expected.
  Effective independent positions saturate at 1/rho = 13. At constant stake-scaled risk growth is
  flat but DRAWDOWN COLLAPSES 13.7% -> 3.3%. Levering every level to the same 40% allowance:
  cap 1 gives +2.6% CAGR, cap 30 gives +17.6%. Diversification is worth ~6.8x at identical risk.

TRADING ONE AT A TIME LOSES MONEY (-8.7%): at cap 1 you take whichever signal arrives while free,
  and you are free most often right after a FAST trade, which is disproportionately a quick loss.

=== EXIT ENGINEERING: CLOSED, THEN REOPENED CONDITIONALLY ===
E[R] = lift for EVERY bracket, so exits are neutral on a martingale. Confirmed five ways.
 * trailing +0.008 (my first sim said +0.22 -- I had detected the trail with the bar's HIGH when a
   trailing stop is taken out by the LOW; the measured 0.744 median pullback exposed it)
 * partial take-profit -0.0002
 * NO ARM POINT EXISTS: E[final | peak p] exceeds p at every level, so cutting early never benefits
BUT conditional on entry quality the bracket is NOT neutral: the optimal target moves outward with
confidence (2.5-3.0 on all bars, 5.0 in the top decile; lift +0.11% -> +20.02%). The neutrality
reading was an artefact of averaging over every bar.
The STOP does not adapt: optimal SL is 4.0 ATR in every confidence band, and even at 0.5 pips every
top-15 configuration uses SL 3.0-4.0. Tight stops need a HIGHER TIMEFRAME, not a cheaper broker.

=== SEVENTH DEADLOCK FIXED (WARRANT#455) ===
g_State.totalTrades is restored from the state file; lastTradeResults[] that feeds the win rate is
never persisted. So the guard passed on a count with no results behind it, _drop = 66.7pp tripped
tier-3, and ghost mode activated 100+ times per run. Now gated on g_Risk.recentSampleN.

=== NEXT ===
1. WIN RATE is the only remaining constraint. 53.2% vs 50% fair. 58% roughly triples the engine.
2. MORE INSTRUMENTS raise the rho ceiling above 13 -- gold, indices, remaining majors.
3. HIGHER TIMEFRAME for the cost term; never tested at low spread.
4. Re-run WARRANT#467 at the broker's true all-in figure once known.
5. OPEN DECISION: sizing on the point estimate rather than the Wilson lower bound roughly DOUBLES
   the 100-day result ($132 -> ~$210), at the cost of assuming the edge is not smaller than measured.

Build: SLS(181) + WARRANT#445-450, #455. 0 errors 0 warnings, deployed byte-identical.
Board: 29 automated MET.
